newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends higher on export data, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends higher on export data, weather.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended firmer and contract highs were notched in the deferred contracts on strong weekly export figures and ideas cool, wet weather would further hamper crop development, traders said.
"The export sales were way up from what I thought they would be," a floor trader said.
USDA on Thursday put weekly rice exports at 46,800 tonnes, five percent below the previous week but more than two times the four-week average.
"There is obviously some business out there and we just don't have much rice left in the cash markets," a trader said.

New crop months were up on the six- to 10-day National Weather Service outlook which called for normal to below normal temperatures and above normal precipitation for Arkansas, Louisiana and most of Texas.
"The six- to 10-day offers not much hope for good crop development through the end of the month," one trader said.
Rice ended eight to one cent per cwt higher with July up 4-1/2 at $11.44-1/2.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 300 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 285 lots.
